title: SQLAdmin /admin accepts any tenant's ADMIN (every self-signup owner) and exposes all tenants' data with full edit and delete
description: The SQLAdmin panel at /admin authorizes any user whose role is ADMIN and never checks tenant or a platform-operator flag. Open public signup makes every new store owner an ADMIN of their own tenant. The panel's ModelViews run on the global engine with no tenant scoping and create/edit/delete enabled, so any self-registered tenant owner can log in at /admin and read, modify or delete users, stores, sales, customers and other data belonging to every other tenant, including Store.mp_access_token.
root_cause: The panel's authorization boundary is the tenant-level role ADMIN, not a platform-superuser concept; AdminAuth.login and authenticate check only role == ADMIN and the views are unscoped ModelViews on the global engine, so RLS (default off) provides no backstop.
intended_behavior: Only platform operators (a separate superuser flag, an allowlist, or a network-restricted or disabled panel) reach a cross-tenant admin UI; a tenant ADMIN is confined to their own tenant's data.

trace.description: Public POST /auth/signup; only an IP rate limit (5 per hour) and a honeypot, no invite or approval.
The new user is created with role=UserRole.ADMIN in a freshly created tenant.
Looks up the user by email and password (RLS bypass) and rejects only if role != ADMIN; no tenant, superuser or allowlist check; stores a session token.
Each /admin request is authorized solely by the JWT role claim equalling ADMIN.
Admin(app, engine=engine, base_url='/admin') is mounted unconditionally; ALL_VIEWS added at lines 158-159.

Plain ModelViews with can_create, can_edit and can_delete True and no tenant-scoped query, covering all tenants' users, stores, subscriptions, sales, customers and inventory; StoreAdmin (line 46) excludes only subscription and conditional_shipments so Store.mp_access_token (store.py:124) is viewable and editable.

evidence.description: Only a role check on login; no tenant or platform flag.
authenticate returns True if the token role claim is ADMIN.
Admin panel mounted unconditionally on the global engine.
Signup always creates an ADMIN user.
UserAdmin has edit and delete enabled and is not tenant-filtered; only hashed_password is hidden.
StoreAdmin form excludes only subscription and conditional_shipments.
RLS_ENABLED defaults to False and no non-doc source enables it.
Catch-all location / proxies everything including /admin; there is no /admin block.
The hardened config also proxies everything under location / to the backend; its only deny rule matches wp-admin, not /admin.

conditions.description: Only a self-registered account via public signup (tenant ADMIN); limited to 5 per hour per IP and a honeypot, no approval step.
RLS_ENABLED off by default and no deploy source enables it; admin DB access uses the global engine anyway.
/admin reachable on the API host; source nginx configs proxy all paths and no block, allowlist or env gate for /admin was found.

execution.attacker_perspective: Unauthenticated internet user who can register a new store.
payloads: POST /api/v1/auth/signup with a new email, store name and slug
GET /admin/login then submit the new account's email and password
Browse /admin/user/list, /admin/store/list, /admin/sale/list and open another tenant's Store detail
instructions: On a local dummy instance register two tenants A and B through signup.
Log in to /admin as tenant A's owner.
Open the User, Store, Sale and Customer views and observe tenant B's rows; edit or delete one of B's rows.
execution.observed_result: Source-established (not executed): login accepts any active ADMIN regardless of tenant, the admin views perform unfiltered queries on the global engine with edit and delete enabled, and no source gating of /admin by flag, environment, allowlist or nginx was found.

remediation.strategy: Add a distinct platform-superuser flag (or configured operator email allowlist) checked in AdminAuth.login and authenticate (embedded in the token and re-validated); mount the panel only when explicitly enabled by a settings flag and restrict /admin by IP or VPN in nginx; remove mp_access_token and other secret fields from the Store form and details. Regression tests: a signup-created ADMIN cannot log in to /admin; /admin returns 404 when disabled.

likelihood.reason: Open public signup is the only prerequisite and no source gate on /admin was found.

impact.reason: Cross-tenant read, write and delete of users, stores, sales and customers plus exposure of tenant payment tokens fully defeats tenant isolation.

confidence.reason: Every link (signup creating ADMIN, role-only admin auth, unconditional mount, unscoped editable views, no nginx or env gating) read in current source; residual risk is production infrastructure outside the repo restricting /admin.

title: Scheduled GitHub Actions DB backup stores an unencrypted pg_dump as a 30-day workflow artifact
description: The workflow .github/workflows/backup-database.yml runs daily at 03:00 UTC and on manual dispatch. It runs pg_dump against the repository secret DATABASE_BACKUP_URL, compresses the output with gzip only and uploads the .sql.gz as a GitHub Actions artifact (actions/upload-artifact@v7) with retention-days 30. A full re-read found no encryption step, no if: condition, no table exclusion and no conditional upload. Anyone with read access to the repository's Actions artifacts (collaborators for a private repo; any signed-in GitHub user for a public repo) can download a full plaintext dump (users, password hashes, customer PII, sales). README documents this as the intended flow. deploy/backup_pg.sh, by contrast, age-encrypts. Exploitability depends on facts outside source: README points DATABASE_BACKUP_URL at a Neon database and CLAUDE.md says Neon/Render are legacy and production moved to a VPS Postgres, so the secret may target a dead or demo database or be unset; repository visibility is not stated.
claimed_root_cause: The CI backup job writes a full plaintext database dump to GitHub Actions artifact storage with 30-day retention and never encrypts it, unlike the VPS script, so artifact read access equals full database read access.

trace.description: Daily cron 0 3 * * * (4-6) and manual workflow_dispatch (7-12) start the job with no condition.
pg_dump of the secret DATABASE_BACKUP_URL with no --exclude-table, piped through tee and gzip into backup_<date>.sql.gz (line 34); no encryption.
Only checks file exists, size >= 100 bytes and gzip --test; exports the file name via GITHUB_OUTPUT (65).
actions/upload-artifact uploads the plaintext .sql.gz with retention-days 30 (73) unconditionally.

evidence.description: Output only gzip-compressed; no encryption step in the 91-line workflow and no if: condition.
retention-days: 30 on the plaintext artifact.
README documents GitHub Actions Artifacts as the backup destination, 30-day retention (403) and download instructions (406-411): intended design.
README tells the owner to set the secret to a Neon postgres URL (legacy database).
Pending item to turn off Render/Neon; line 183 says Neon was abandoned (quota exceeded) and line 206 that production is a new empty Postgres on the VPS.
Contrast: the production VPS backup is gzip then age-encrypted with an age header check at line 23.
MIT license badge; nothing in source states repo visibility.

blockers: Repository visibility (public vs private) and the collaborator list are not in source; artifact read access depends on both.
Whether the secret DATABASE_BACKUP_URL is set in repository or environment secrets is not visible in source.
Which database the secret points to (legacy Neon, demo, or the new VPS production database) is not visible in source; production Postgres publishes no port so the runner may not reach it.
Whether the Database Backup workflow is enabled and whether recent scheduled runs succeeded with unexpired artifacts is not visible in source.
Organization or repo-level artifact retention and download policy are not visible in source.

validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed checks in the GitHub UI, no live probing: (1) Settings > General: confirm repository visibility, and open the repo logged out to see whether Actions runs and artifacts are listed; (2) Settings > Collaborators and teams: list everyone with read access; (3) Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions: check whether DATABASE_BACKUP_URL exists, its last-updated date and which host it uses (Neon, VPS or other) without revealing the value; (4) Actions > Database Backup: confirm the workflow is enabled, the last scheduled run succeeded and backup_*.sql.gz artifacts are listed with unexpired dates; (5) if artifacts exist, check whether they hold real production data; (6) if real data is present and the repo is public or has broad collaborators, delete the artifacts, rotate database credentials and any stored provider tokens, and encrypt dumps with age or gpg before upload (or drop the workflow in favour of deploy/backup_pg.sh with offsite copy).
validation_plan.local: Inspect repository history only: git log -p on .github/workflows/backup-database.yml for any past encryption step, and read repository visibility with the owner's own authenticated gh (gh api repos/vscardoso/fitness-store-management --jq .private). Do not run the workflow.

title: Signup-issued stateless refresh JWT is accepted as an access bearer token for 7 days and cannot be revoked
description: get_current_user decodes the bearer JWT and checks only signature, exp and the presence of sub; it never reads the type claim (both token factories stamp access or refresh, and verify_token_type exists but has no callers). POST /auth/signup returns an access JWT and a refresh JWT created with create_refresh_token({'sub': user.id}); that refresh JWT is stateless, not stored in the database, and used as Authorization: Bearer authenticates the user for REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRE_DAYS=7 instead of the 30 minutes of an access token. Logout is a no-op and JWTs are not tracked, so it cannot be revoked. Same principal's own session and needs a prior token leak, so this is near the hardening threshold. Login-issued refresh tokens are opaque and DB-tracked and are not affected.
root_cause: get_current_user does not enforce token purpose (type == access) and the signup flow issues a refresh token as a self-contained signed JWT with no server-side record or version binding.
intended_behavior: Only access-type tokens authenticate API requests; refresh credentials are usable only at the refresh endpoint and are revocable, as login-issued refresh tokens already are.

trace.description: create_refresh_token({'sub': str(user.id)}) mints a stateless 7-day HS256 JWT with type=refresh and no DB record; returned in SignupResponse.refresh_token (line 148) next to the access token (147).
Payload gets exp = now + REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRE_DAYS (7) and type=refresh, signed with the same SECRET_KEY and ALGORITHM as access tokens.
jwt.decode with pinned algorithms validates only signature and exp; the type claim is never examined.
After the sub check (65-67) the user is loaded by id and the tenant set (line 91); the request proceeds authenticated with the refresh JWT; no iat, password-change or token-version check.

evidence.description: Decode checks only signature and exp.
Access tokens carry type=access, so a distinguishing claim exists but is unused.
verify_token_type is defined and has no callers in backend/.
Signup refresh token is a stateless JWT with sub only, not persisted.
REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRE_DAYS = 7 versus ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES = 30 at line 49.
Logout is a TODO no-op with no blacklist.

conditions.description: Attacker must already hold the signup response body or stored refresh_token (client storage, logs, proxy); same-user session, no privilege gained beyond that user's own.
Applies only to sessions created through /auth/signup; login-issued refresh tokens are opaque and DB-tracked.
Usable until the 7-day exp; deactivation is still honoured by get_current_active_user, but logout and password change do not revoke it.

execution.attacker_perspective: Holder of a leaked refresh_token from a signup response whose 30-minute access token has expired.
instructions: Locally call POST /auth/signup with dummy data and keep the returned refresh_token.
After the access token expires, call GET /auth/me with the refresh_token as Bearer.
Call POST /auth/logout and repeat; the request still authenticates.
execution.observed_result: Source-established (not executed): get_current_user accepts any validly signed, unexpired JWT with a sub claim regardless of type, loads the user and sets the tenant; no server-side state can invalidate it before exp.

remediation.strategy: In get_current_user reject any token whose type != access (use verify_token_type) immediately after decode; issue signup's refresh token the same way login does (opaque, DB-tracked) so logout and revocation work. Regression tests: a signup refresh JWT on /auth/me returns 401; a signup access token still returns 200.

likelihood.reason: Requires a prior leak of a credential the user already holds and applies only to signup-issued sessions.

impact.reason: Same-principal session; extends an unrevocable credential from 30 minutes to 7 days and defeats access/refresh separation; no cross-user or cross-tenant boundary crossed.

confidence.reason: Missing type check, stateless signup refresh JWT and no-op logout are clear in source; real-world value is limited because access JWTs are also unrevocable and a prior leak is required.

title: Unauthenticated Mercado Pago OAuth callback trusts a raw tenant_id in state and overwrites any tenant's payment token
description: GET /api/v1/mp-connect/callback has no authentication. It takes the tenant from the unsigned state query parameter, which /mp-connect/url sets to the plain tenant id, exchanges code with the platform's MP client credentials and unconditionally UPDATEs that tenant's Store row with the resulting access token, refresh token, MP user id and expiry. An attacker authorizes the platform's MP app with their own MP account, then replays the code to the callback with state set to a victim tenant id. In the default production configuration (PIX_PROVIDER=mercadopago) the victim's later PIX QR codes are created under the attacker's MP account, so payments are credited to the attacker.
root_cause: The OAuth state parameter is used as a direct tenant selector instead of a CSRF/session-bound nonce; the callback has no authenticated principal, no signed or stored state, and no check that the completing party started the flow; it runs on get_db_unscoped and overwrites any existing connection.
intended_behavior: Only an authenticated tenant ADMIN who started the connect flow may bind a Mercado Pago account to that tenant; state must be a single-use, expiring, server-verifiable value bound to tenant and user.

trace.description: Only Query(code), Query(state) and get_db_unscoped; no get_current_user; the permission matrix applies only through get_current_* dependencies.
tenant_id = int(state) with no signature, nonce, cookie or session check.
Exchanges the supplied code at MP_TOKEN_URL with the platform client_id/secret; the token belongs to whichever MP account authorized the app.
UPDATE Store WHERE id=tenant_id SET mp_access_token, mp_refresh_token, mp_user_id, mp_token_expires_at and pix_provider; unconditional, overwrites an existing connection.

evidence.description: /mp-connect/url (authenticated) emits state={tenant_id} raw and exposes MP_CLIENT_ID and redirect_uri in the authorize URL (46-54).
Callback uses the RLS-bypass session; docstring at 68-69 states no JWT auth.
_get_mp_token_for_tenant returns Store.mp_access_token when set (226-227).
create_pix_payment passes the tenant's stored token as mp_token when provider == mercadopago; POST /pdv/pix/{sale_id} passes no provider so the default applies.
Provider defaults to the global PIX_PROVIDER, not Store.pix_provider (never read on this path), so the token overwrite is what redirects payments.
Production compose default is PIX_PROVIDER=mercadopago, so the stored per-tenant token is used for PIX creation.

conditions.description: MP_CLIENT_ID and MP_CLIENT_SECRET configured and the MP app redirect URI is APP_URL/api/v1/mp-connect/callback; neither is set in the repo deploy files, so this assumes the OAuth feature is enabled.

Impact on PIX needs the global PIX_PROVIDER to be mercadopago (prod compose default). Via create_pix_start a victim store with a pix_key is routed to generic PIX and is unaffected; POST /pdv/pix/{sale_id} uses the default provider regardless.
Mercado Pago must pass an arbitrary state through to the redirect and accept a code for the legit redirect_uri (standard OAuth); not testable from source.
Attacker needs the victim tenant id; ids are small sequential integers.
No platform authentication on the callback; the attacker needs their own Mercado Pago account and the public MP_CLIENT_ID.

execution.attacker_perspective: Anonymous internet user with an ordinary Mercado Pago account.
payloads: GET /api/v1/mp-connect/callback?code=<code from the attacker's own MP authorization of the platform app>&state=<victim_tenant_id>
instructions: On a local dummy instance with a stubbed MP token endpoint and two tenants (1 attacker, 2 victim), call GET /mp-connect/callback?code=X&state=2 with no Authorization header.
Observe Store 2 now holds the stubbed access token.
Create a PIX payment for tenant 2 and observe _get_mp_token_for_tenant returns the injected token.
execution.observed_result: Source-established (not executed): the callback performs no authentication or state verification, exchanges the supplied code with platform credentials and updates Store.mp_access_token, mp_refresh_token, mp_user_id, mp_token_expires_at and pix_provider for Store.id == int(state) on an RLS-bypassing session; PIX creation later reads that stored token.

remediation.strategy: Mint a signed, short-lived, single-use state in /mp-connect/url (tenant_id, user_id, random nonce stored server-side or bound to a browser cookie, exp, purpose); in /callback verify signature, expiry and nonce and consume it before taking the tenant from the verified payload; reject otherwise; optionally refuse to overwrite an existing connection without an explicit reconnect. Regression tests: forged integer state is rejected with no UPDATE; expired or replayed state rejected; valid state for tenant A cannot change tenant B.

likelihood.reason: No platform account needed and trivial once the OAuth app is configured; depends on MP_CLIENT_ID being set and MP passing state through; tenant ids enumerable.

impact.reason: Cross-tenant overwrite of a payment credential; in the default prod PIX_PROVIDER=mercadopago configuration victim PIX payments are created under the attacker's MP account, diverting funds.

confidence.reason: Source trace complete with no preventing control; Mercado Pago behaviors (state passthrough, code usable for the legit redirect_uri) are not verifiable from source and exploitation depends on global PIX_PROVIDER being mercadopago.

title: POST /pdv/orders lets any tenant flip another tenant's sale to PENDING, so the stale-sale job cancels it and reverts stock and loyalty
description: POST /api/v1/pdv/orders takes sale_id from the request body. PDVService.create_order only checks that the terminal belongs to the caller's tenant, then calls the provider's create_payment. The manual provider (also the factory fallback for rede, getnet, pagseguro, sumup and any unknown provider string) runs UPDATE sales SET status=PENDING WHERE id=:sale_id with no tenant filter and no existence check; the Mercado Pago provider overwrites payment_reference by id alone. The scheduler job auto_cancel_stale_pending_sales (RLS-bypass session, every 5 minutes) cancels every non-PIX PENDING sale older than 30 minutes via SaleService.cancel_sale, reverting FIFO stock, loyalty and spend. A user in one tenant can therefore tamper with and then destroy sales in another tenant. The competing claim that the path is dead because of payload.get was refuted: create_order uses attribute access and no .get call exists on that path.
root_cause: The sale_id in the request body is trusted; provider UPDATEs are keyed by Sale.id only, so the tenant check made on the terminal is never applied to the sale, while the neighbouring status, cancel and refund methods filter by tenant.
intended_behavior: create_payment acts only on a sale belonging to the calling tenant, preferably PENDING or unpaid with a matching total; a foreign sale fails with the same not-found response as a missing sale.

trace.description: Takes PDVOrderRequest (sale_id, terminal_id, total_amount) from the body and passes the model unchanged to the service (273); legacy alias POST /pdv/payment at 484-491; CASHIER and above (permissions.py:59).
Only terminal.tenant_id == tenant_id is checked (161-163); then get_terminal_provider(terminal.provider).create_payment(sale_id=payload.sale_id, ...) with attribute access (165-177).
Only mercadopago, stone and cielo map to their own classes; every other string including manual falls through to ManualTerminalProvider (28-31).
update(Sale).where(Sale.id == sale_id).values(status=PENDING) committed at line 66 with no tenant filter and no existence check.

Selects PENDING non-PIX active sales older than 30 minutes across all tenants (761-768) and calls cancel_sale with the sale's own tenant_id (777-782), reversing FIFO stock and loyalty and setting CANCELLED; job runs every 5 minutes on a bypass_on session (core/scheduler.py:86-96).

evidence.description: create_order uses payload.terminal_id and payload.sale_id (161, 169) with no dict .get call, disproving the dead-path claim.
PDVOrderRequest has sale_id: int, terminal_id: int and total_amount: float with no ownership validation.
Unscoped UPDATE on sales; other methods in the file (get_payment_status 87, cancel_payment 116) filter by tenant_id.
update(Sale).where(Sale.id == sale_id).values(payment_reference=mp_order_id) with no tenant filter; second unscoped write, needs a working MP terminal.
Writes to /pdv/terminals require ADMIN, which limits who can create a manual terminal, but signup gives every new tenant an ADMIN.
create_terminal accepts an arbitrary provider string such as manual for a terminal in the caller's own tenant.
cancel_sale rejects only already CANCELLED sales, so a tampered COMPLETED sale (now PENDING) is cancelled with stock and loyalty reverted.
RLS_ENABLED defaults to False; no RLS setting under deploy/.

conditions.description: A valid account: self-signup gives an ADMIN of a fresh tenant (auth.py:319) or any existing tenant ADMIN.

ADMIN once to create a terminal with provider manual in the attacker's own tenant (permissions.py:47); then CASHIER or higher can call POST /pdv/orders. No ADMIN action if the attacker tenant already has a non-MP, non-Stone, non-Cielo terminal.
RLS_ENABLED false (default, not enabled in deploy); with RLS on the request-session UPDATE would not see other tenants' rows.
Victim sale is non-PIX, active and older than 30 minutes; ids are sequential and guessable.
The APScheduler job runs every 5 minutes and must be enabled; harm lands at the next run.

execution.attacker_perspective: A signed-in ADMIN of their own tenant B targeting a completed non-PIX sale in tenant A.
payloads: POST /api/v1/pdv/terminals {"name":"x","external_id":"x1","provider":"manual"} (once, as ADMIN of tenant B)
POST /api/v1/pdv/orders {"sale_id":<tenant A sale id>,"terminal_id":<tenant B manual terminal id>,"total_amount":1.0}
instructions: On a local dummy deployment with two tenants create a COMPLETED cash sale in tenant A older than 30 minutes.
As tenant B ADMIN create a manual terminal then POST /pdv/orders with tenant A's sale id and the manual terminal.
Read tenant A's sale: status is pending; run auto_cancel_stale_pending_sales and observe it become cancelled with stock restored.
execution.observed_result: Source-established (not executed): the manual provider commits status=PENDING for the given id regardless of tenant and returns 200; the scheduler job then selects that sale and cancels it using the sale's own tenant_id, reverting FIFO stock and loyalty.

remediation.strategy: In PDVService.create_order load the sale with Sale.id == payload.sale_id AND Sale.tenant_id == tenant_id and raise not-found otherwise; require the sale to be PENDING/draft and total_amount to equal sale.total_amount; add Sale.tenant_id == tenant_id to the UPDATE in manual.py:62 and mercadopago.py:313 and to similar writes keyed by sale id alone (pdv_service lines near 906-908, 1068, 1086, 1103). Regression test: tenant B calling POST /pdv/orders with tenant A's sale_id gets an error and the sale status is unchanged.

likelihood.reason: Self-signup account plus one terminal creation; sale ids guessable; job's 30-minute age gate met by any older sale; depends on the scheduler running.

impact.reason: Cross-tenant write that changes another tenant's sale status and, through the job, cancels the sale and reverses stock and loyalty: integrity of financial records across tenants.

confidence.reason: Whole path read in the working tree; payload is a pydantic model used by attribute access, provider UPDATE has no tenant filter, factory falls back to manual, job criteria match a flipped non-PIX sale. Residual: runtime RLS state and scheduler running.

title: Mercado Pago webhook accepts unauthenticated forged order events: signature check fails open and the production compose never supplies MP_WEBHOOK_SECRET
description: POST /api/v1/pdv/webhooks/mp is anonymous and uses get_db_unscoped. Its only control, verify_webhook_signature, returns True whenever MP_WEBHOOK_SECRET is empty (default empty). deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml gives the backend only an explicit environment list and MP_WEBHOOK_SECRET is not on it; deploy/.env.prod.example does not mention it. In the documented deployment the signature check is therefore off. For topics order and point_integration_wh, process_webhook trusts the body external_reference sale_<id> and calls _confirm_sale, _cancel_sale or _refund_sale with no Mercado Pago API call and no tenant filter, so an anonymous caller can mark any tenant's PENDING sale paid, cancel PENDING sales or refund COMPLETED ones. Topics payment and merchant_order re-query the MP API and are not forgeable this way. Even with a secret set, the HMAC covers only data.id, x-request-id and ts (not the body; no ts freshness check).
root_cause: The signature verifier fails open on a missing secret and the compose file never passes the secret to the container; the order and point_integration_wh handlers treat unauthenticated body fields as proof of payment using an unscoped Sale lookup by id.
intended_behavior: Only Mercado Pago may drive sale state transitions: reject webhooks when no secret is configured, verify the signature, and confirm payment state from the MP API or a stored order id bound to the tenant's sale.

trace.description: Anonymous POST /pdv/webhooks/mp on get_db_unscoped with no auth dependency.
If MP_WEBHOOK_SECRET is empty it logs a warning and returns True (lines 561-563).
For topic order (dispatched at line 497) reads data.external_reference sale_<id> and status from the body and parses the integer id; point_integration_wh (502-509) does the same.

select(Sale).where(Sale.id == sale_id) with no tenant filter; a PENDING sale becomes COMPLETED, an audit row is written and payment approved is signalled (703-716). _cancel_sale (718) and _refund_sale (736) are likewise unscoped.

evidence.description: MP_WEBHOOK_SECRET defaults to the empty string.
MP_WEBHOOK_SECRET= is left empty in the example env.
Comment says the container receives only the variables listed; the backend environment block (lines 30-50) lists MP_ACCESS_TOKEN (line 39) but no MP_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
Lists MP_ACCESS_TOKEN= only; no MP_WEBHOOK_SECRET entry.
HMAC manifest built only from id, request-id and ts; body not covered and ts freshness not checked.
The payment topic re-queries the MP API and checks the amount, which is why only order and point_integration_wh are body-trusting.
All paths including /api/v1/pdv/webhooks/mp are proxied to the backend with no auth or allowlist.

conditions.description: MP_WEBHOOK_SECRET is empty in the running backend, the state produced by the shipped docker-compose.prod.yml. Differs only if the operator edited the compose file or baked a backend/.env into the image on the VPS (not visible in the repo).
A target sale must be PENDING for confirm or cancel; ids are sequential and the lookup is not tenant-scoped.
Endpoint reachable by an anonymous caller through the public nginx for api.provadorfit.com.br.

execution.attacker_perspective: Anonymous internet client with no account and no Mercado Pago relationship.
instructions: Locally with MP_WEBHOOK_SECRET unset, create a PENDING sale in a dummy tenant.
Send the JSON body to /api/v1/pdv/webhooks/mp with no x-signature.
Observe _confirm_sale move the sale from PENDING to COMPLETED; order.canceled or order.refunded actions cancel a PENDING sale or refund a COMPLETED one.
execution.observed_result: Source-established (not executed): with an empty MP_WEBHOOK_SECRET the endpoint returns 200 and, for an order body naming an existing PENDING sale, updates it to COMPLETED regardless of tenant, writes a PDV_SALE_CONFIRMED audit row and signals payment approved. No Mercado Pago payment is checked.

remediation.strategy: Make verify_webhook_signature fail closed when MP_WEBHOOK_SECRET is empty (or refuse to start in production without it); add MP_WEBHOOK_SECRET to the compose environment list and deploy/.env.prod.example; reject stale ts; make order and point_integration_wh confirm via the MP API or match a stored mp_order_id with a tenant-bound lookup before _confirm_sale. Regression test: an unsigned or secret-less webhook with an order body does not change a PENDING sale.

likelihood.reason: Anonymous, one unsigned request; the shipped compose does not forward the secret, so the check is off in the documented deployment.

impact.reason: Unauthenticated party can mark any tenant's PENDING sale paid, cancel PENDING sales or refund COMPLETED ones, defeating the webhook authentication control across tenants.

confidence.reason: Code path and deploy wiring fully visible; medium because the real VPS .env.prod or any image-baked backend/.env cannot be inspected.

title: Unauthenticated Stone, Cielo and Cielo PIX webhooks flip any tenant's sale to COMPLETED
description: POST /api/v1/pdv/webhooks/stone, /cielo and /cielo-pix are registered on the public api_router with no authentication, signature, shared secret or IP check, and use get_db_unscoped (RLS bypass). An anonymous caller who supplies a sequential sale id, a Cielo order id stored in payment_reference, or a txid of the form VENDA<id> can mark a sale from any tenant COMPLETED. Stone does this with no status or tenant guard, so it also moves CANCELLED or REFUNDED sales to COMPLETED. Cielo PIX confirms any PENDING sale whether or not a PixTransaction exists. title: Legacy Baileys WhatsApp webhook is unauthenticated in the shipped production deploy and reads Product and Customer data across all tenants
description: POST /webhooks/whatsapp checks a shared token only when the BOT_TOKEN module constant is non-empty. BOT_TOKEN is read with os.getenv at import time; deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml passes the container an explicit list of variables and WHATSAPP_BOT_TOKEN is not on it, so the token is empty and the check skipped; any internet caller reaches the handlers through nginx. The handlers run on get_db_unscoped and their queries have no tenant filter: product search lists active product names and prices from every tenant, and the wishlist handler looks up a Customer by phone with LIKE on a caller-controlled from_number (the % and _ wildcards work) and replies with the customer's first name and wishlist product names.
root_cause: Three flaws combine: a fail-open token check (if BOT_TOKEN and ...), a prod compose that omits WHATSAPP_BOT_TOKEN (pydantic env_file does not populate os.environ), and tenant-agnostic queries on an RLS-bypassing session.
intended_behavior: Only the store's own Baileys bot presenting the shared secret may call the webhook, and lookups are limited to the one tenant the bot serves with an exact normalized phone match.

The legacy whatsapp_router is included unconditionally outside /api/v1; nginx location / (deploy/protecao/provador-api.site:33) proxies all paths with only rate limits.

instructions: Locally with WHATSAPP_BOT_TOKEN unset, seed two dummy tenants with distinct products and one customer with a wishlist in tenant B.
Send the first payload with no X-Bot-Token; the reply lists up to 5 active products with prices from any tenant.
Send the second payload with a digit pattern using wildcards, narrowing until exactly one customer matches; the reply contains the first name and up to 10 wishlist product names.
execution.observed_result: Source-established (not executed): with BOT_TOKEN empty the 401 check is skipped; with RLS bypassed and no tenant predicate the product search returns names and prices from all tenants and the wishlist handler returns the matched customer's first name and wishlist items from any tenant. Multi-match patterns raise an unhandled MultipleResultsFound.

remediation.strategy: Fail closed: refuse every request (503/401) when the token is unset and compare with hmac.compare_digest; read the token through settings; add WHATSAPP_BOT_TOKEN to docker-compose.prod.yml and deploy/.env.prod.example, or remove the router from main.py if the Baileys bot is retired; pin a tenant id for the bot and add tenant_id predicates to the Product and Customer queries; replace LIKE with an exact comparison on the normalized phone (or escape wildcards) and use a tenant-scoped unique lookup. Regression tests: no valid token gives 401 even when unset; handlers return only the configured tenant's rows.
